objectives.topic_title: Introduction to Algorithms, Programming, and Compilers
objectives.summary: Design and express sequential everyday algorithms in plain prose or diagrams.

objectives.topic_title: Introduction to Algorithms, Programming, and Compilers
objectives.summary: Describe how source code is authored, checked by a compiler, and executed, including IDE support.

objectives.topic_title: Introduction to Algorithms, Programming, and Compilers
objectives.summary: Distinguish compile-time syntax errors, logic errors found by testing, run-time failures, and exceptions.
Choose between primitive and reference data-type categories for a stated problem requirement.
Declare typed primitive variables (int, double, boolean) to store numeric and truth values.
Write and trace console output statements using System.out.print and System.out.println.
Construct and evaluate string literals including escape sequences for quotes, backslashes, and newlines.
Write and evaluate int and double arithmetic expressions using +, -, *, /, %, precedence rules, and integer division by zero.
Initialize and update variables with = expressions, including null references, and trace stored values.
Write Java code that reads input supplied to a program.
Apply explicit (int) and (double) casts and implicit widening in arithmetic, including truncation and rounding patterns.
Identify integer overflow when 32-bit int calculations exceed Integer.MIN_VALUE through Integer.MAX_VALUE.
Explain floating-point round-off errors caused by finite double representation precision.
Write and trace compound assignment (+=, -=, *=, /=, %=) and postfix ++ and -- variable updates.
Read library and API documentation to determine a class's data attributes, methods, and package grouping.
Document code behavior, preconditions, and postconditions with line, block, and Javadoc comments ignored by the compiler.
Select the matching method to invoke from documentation and method parameter signatures.
Explain method invocation rules for void and non-void methods, call-by-value arguments, overloading, and control flow return.
Invoke static class methods with the class name and dot operator and trace their return values.
Write and evaluate expressions calling Math.abs, Math.pow, Math.sqrt, and scaled Math.random ranges.
Explain classes as object blueprints, Object as Java's universal superclass, and conceptual superclass/subclass relationships without designing hierarchies.
Declare variables of reference types that hold references to objects.
Match a constructor call to its signature among potentially overloaded constructors.
Declare reference variables typed for objects or initialized to null.
Instantiate objects with new, passing constructor arguments by value and tracing constructor execution.
Invoke instance methods on object references with the dot operator, trace outcomes, and recognize NullPointerException on null targets.
Create immutable String objects, concatenate strings with primitive or toString values, and trace results.
Invoke String methods (length, substring, indexOf, equals, compareTo) and recognize out-of-bounds index exceptions.
Express everyday algorithms combining sequence, conditional choice, and repetition in prose or diagrams.
Write and evaluate Boolean expressions that compare primitive values or reference identity with == and !=, and test numeric ordering with <, >, <=, and >=.
Implement and trace one-way if and two-way if-else branching statements.
Implement and trace nested if and multiway if-else-if selection chains.
Construct and trace compound Boolean logic with !, &&, and ||, operator precedence, and short-circuit evaluation.
Prove Boolean equivalence using truth tables and De Morgan's laws.
Compare object references for alias identity (==, !=, null) versus attribute equality (equals).
Recognize problems needing iteration and diagnose zero-iteration conditions, infinite loops, and off-by-one bugs.
Write and trace while loop repetition governed by a pre-checked Boolean condition.
Write and trace for loops with header initialization, guard, and update, and convert between for and while.
Implement and trace standard non-collection algorithms for divisibility, integer digits, counts, min/max, and sums or averages.
Implement and trace iterative algorithms that search, count substrings, and reverse strings.
Implement and trace nested loops where the inner loop finishes completely on each outer iteration.
Trace loops to count statement executions and compare iterative run-time efficiency informally.
Plan class-based programs in prose or diagrams specifying data attributes, procedural decomposition, and method behaviors.
Analyze software reliability, beneficial and harmful societal, economic, and cultural impacts, and open-source versus proprietary licensing.
Apply public and private access modifiers to classes, instance fields, constructors, and methods to enforce encapsulation.
Declare private instance fields, initialize object state in constructors (copying mutable arguments), and apply default constructor rules.
Author void mutators and typed non-void accessor or computation methods using primitive parameters passed by value and return flow.

objectives.topic_title: Methods: Passing and Returning References of an Object
objectives.summary: Write and trace methods taking and returning object references, observing aliasing, mutable state effects, and same-class private access.
Write static class methods that operate on static state and class helpers without direct instance state access.
Declare shared static class variables and final constants with appropriate visibility.
Determine variable visibility across blocks, constructors, methods, and parameters, including local shadowing of instance fields.
Use this within instance methods and constructors to refer to or pass the active receiver object (unavailable in static methods).

objectives.topic_title: Ethical and Social Issues Around Data Collection
objectives.summary: Explain personal privacy hazards from collecting and retaining user data and a developer's responsibility to safeguard privacy.

objectives.topic_title: Ethical and Social Issues Around Data Collection
objectives.summary: Identify risks from algorithmic bias, biased collection practices, and incomplete or inaccurate data sets.

objectives.topic_title: Ethical and Social Issues Around Data Collection
objectives.summary: Evaluate whether a data set is fit to answer a specific problem without invalid extrapolation.
Represent everyday data-set workflows and tabular or charted structures in prose or diagrams prior to coding.
Create fixed-size 1D primitive or object arrays via new or initializer lists, index with [], check .length, and handle bounds errors.
Traverse 1D arrays with indexed for/while loops and enhanced for loops, distinguishing element-variable copies from object state updates.
Implement and trace 1D array algorithms for extrema, totals, quantifiers, counts, adjacent pairs, duplicates, shifts or rotations, and reversal.
Read persistent text files using java.io.File, Scanner, throws IOException, hasNext/next methods, literal String.split, and close.
Use immutable Integer and Double wrappers with their primitives through boxing and unboxing. Use parseInt and parseDouble to parse strings into primitive numbers.
Create parameterized ArrayList<E> collections from java.util and trace size, add, get, set, and remove.
Traverse ArrayList collections safely, handling index shifts on deletion, IndexOutOfBoundsException, and ConcurrentModificationException.
Implement and trace ArrayList manipulation algorithms (including insertion and deletion) and parallel multi-collection traversals.
Represent rectangular 2D arrays as arrays of row arrays, index via [row][col], inspect row and column lengths, and handle bounds errors.
Traverse 2D arrays in row-major, column-major, or custom orders using nested indexed or enhanced for loops.
Implement and trace 2D array algorithms across full grids, specific rows or columns, or subsections.
Implement and trace linear search across 1D arrays, ArrayList instances, and row-by-row 2D arrays.
Trace each pass of iterative selection sort and insertion sort on arrays and ArrayList collections.
Trace recursive methods with base cases, per-call local variables, and iterative equivalence without authoring recursive code.
Trace recursive traversals over strings, arrays, and ArrayList collections.
Trace each step of iterative or recursive binary search on sorted collections and compare efficiency to linear search.
Trace recursive divide-and-merge steps of merge sort on arrays and ArrayList collections.
